evals.prompt: Draft a message for this proposed commit in result.md. The diff adds a login command with a working CLI entrypoint and also fixes an unrelated spelling mistake in the project introduction. The author proposes 'feat: improve the project'. I only want a message and any useful feedback, not changes to code or history.
evals.expected_output: Describe both concerns honestly and flag their unrelated scope without doing decomposition or refusing to draft.
expectations: The proposed message does not hide either concern behind a generic improvement claim
Author-facing feedback identifies the unrelated changes and suggests separate planning
Produces a draft without creating commits or attempting history restructuring

evals.prompt: Improve this commit message in result.md. Original subject: 'feat(cli): add hello greeting'. The commit was amended and now adds a CLI with hello and goodbye subcommands, both wired into the dispatcher. This is the complete resulting diff. Draft only.
evals.expected_output: Describe the resulting greeting CLI rather than only the original hello addition or the goodbye amendment.
expectations: The subject accurately covers the complete resulting CLI change
Uses an imperative Conventional Commits subject
Does not execute an amend or describe only the most recent delta

evals.prompt: Write a commit message in result.md for a consistent rename from tokenOffset to byteOffset; it clarifies the unit and changes no behavior. Draft only.
evals.expected_output: A specific Conventional Commits subject, with no unnecessary body or execution workflow.
expectations: Uses a concrete imperative subject accurately describing the rename

evals.prompt: Draft a commit subject and body in result.md, without creating or amending commits. This commit moves existing campaign body declarations beneath pr. Headings, templates, generated values, and render order remain identical. A later commit adds title configuration. Existing body: 'Move the body fields under pr without changing rendering.' Use only these supplied facts.
evals.expected_output: A concise ownership refactor explanation names the preserved rendering properties.
expectations: Uses an imperative Conventional Commits subject describing the structural move
Names relevant preserved rendering properties without claiming title support
Does not create or amend commits or invent test results

evals.prompt: Draft a commit subject and body in result.md from this before/after pseudocode. Before: result = execute(); push(result); pr = publish(result); saveExecution(result, chargedAttempt); savePublication(pr). After: result = execute(); push(result); saveExecution(result, chargedAttempt); pr = publish(result); savePublication(pr). Each function can throw; later calls do not run after a throw. saveExecution stores completed work and its charged attempt on the task. publish creates or edits its PR. The current body is 'Checkpoint execution before publication so failed publication is recoverable.' Draft only; no git mutations.
evals.expected_output: Explain the concrete ordering and condition recovery on a successful checkpoint.
expectations: Explains the old publication-failure consequence before relying on checkpoint terminology, so a reader can understand why changing the order helps
Explains push, checkpoint, publication ordering and recovery from publication failure
Does not guarantee durability when the checkpoint fails
Distinguishes execution evidence from publication evidence
Uses a specific Conventional Commits subject and does not mutate history

evals.prompt: Review this proposed commit message against the supplied facts and write result.md. Subject: 'feat(harness): switch actions to the second provider'. Body: 'Use the new provider for every action. Tests pass.' Actual commit: adds and exports an injectable provider implementation; action factories still use the original provider. Tests assert decoding and cleanup with mocks, but no run result is known. The child commit switches defaults. Draft a corrected message only.
evals.expected_output: Correct both scope and validation claims at this commit's tree.
expectations: Subject and body describe implementing a provider without claiming adoption
Removes the unsupported tests-pass claim without inventing replacement results
Keeps the message understandable without the child or PR discussion
Does not rewrite history
